The route

Your AI requests a tool. GateRook checks the endpoint policy, resolves credentials locally, and calls the configured service.

Understand the request flow

Ask your AI

Find recent order 48213 errors in Google Cloud Logging and explain the sequence.

logs_search · arguments
{
  "connection": "stage-cloud-logs",
  "query": "severity>=ERROR AND SEARCH(\"48213\")",
  "from": "-15m",
  "to": "now",
  "limit": 20
}
Example result
{
  "backend": "gcp-logging",
  "entries": [
    {
      "timestamp": "2026-10-22T12:29:00Z",
      "severity": "ERROR",
      "message": "Payment authorization timed out for order 48213"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "truncated": false
}

Sample configuration and output, not a live connection. Replace example values with your environment. Tool names here are connector names; the endpoint may expose a connection-specific name.

Put context to work

What you can do with Google Cloud Logging and AI

Read a Kubernetes workload’s logs

Use a fixed k8s_container and namespace filter, then investigate specific error messages without opening unrelated application logs.

Investigate structured events

Ask the AI to inspect returned jsonPayload or other structured fields and compare events by an application identifier.

Use a dedicated log view

Point the connection to an existing log view to narrow its accessible data independently of the query supplied by the agent.

From service to MCP

How to connect Google Cloud Logging

GateRook must be running on a computer that can reach your service. Open Connections, choose Add connection, and select Logs. Give the connection a name and environment.

New to GateRook? Start with the full setup guide.
  1. 01

    Prepare the Google Cloud identity

    Use gcloud auth application-default login on the GateRook computer for ADC, or prepare a service account key for the connection. Grant read access only to the intended logs. Configure impersonation permissions if you use a target service account.

  2. 02

    Choose resources and an enforced filter

    Open Connections, Add connection and GCP Cloud Logging. Select the resource names, identity source and optional impersonation target. Add an always-on scope filter for the service or namespace.

  3. 03

    Test and save the connection

    Run Test connection and finish Add to endpoint. Verify a short Logging query language search in Playground before using it from an AI app.

  4. 04

    Choose the endpoint and tool modes

    Add the tested connection to an endpoint. In Tools & policies, enable only the tools needed for the task. Start with Read only where supported; use Approval for any selected mutation and leave other tools Off. A connection alone does not grant an AI client access.

  5. 05

    Connect your AI and verify the first call

    In Clients, choose your AI app and endpoint, review the connection details, and connect. Try this guide’s example in Playground before asking your AI. Open Activity to inspect the tool, target, decision and returned result. The getting started guide covers this shared flow.

Connection settings

Configure Google Cloud Logging in GateRook

These are example values for the connection form. Enter credentials into GateRook’s secret fields, not into an AI prompt. Requirements and alternatives are noted per field.

Google Cloud Logging connection configuration
SettingExampleHow to use it
Connector typeGCP Cloud LoggingThe Google Cloud backend of the Logs connector.
Name / environmentstage-cloud-logs / stageKeep environments and access scopes recognizable.
Resource namesprojects/orders-stageUse project, folder, organization, billing account or supported log view resource names. A log view provides the tightest scope.
Credentials sourceadcUse Application Default Credentials on this computer, or select serviceAccountKey and enter the JSON key in GateRook.
Impersonategw-reader@orders-stage.iam.gserviceaccount.comOptional service account impersonation. The source identity needs permission to impersonate the target.
Always add this filterresource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.namespace_name="orders"A fixed filter applied in addition to the agent query.

Know what you expose

Google Cloud Logging tools and access boundaries

The connector determines what is possible. Endpoint modes and connection policies determine what a particular AI client may use.

Available tools and access behavior
ToolPurposeAccess behavior
logs_searchSearch a bounded time range in the backend query language, with a cursor for older results.Read only
logs_tailRead new log entries since a cursor, waiting up to eight seconds for another page.Read only

Before you enable access

  • This integration reads logs. It does not edit entries, change retention or administer the logging service.
  • The connection scope, environment policy and result limits all apply. A truncated page is only part of the evidence.
  • Log messages may contain application data or sensitive payloads. Scope the source and review the data your AI app is permitted to receive.
  • Google Cloud IAM and log-view permissions remain authoritative. Configuring a resource does not grant access to it.
  • The connection includes a quota-per-minute setting for entries.list calls. Broad searches can still consume project API quota.

GateRook stores local connection secrets encrypted and resolves them for connectors. Allowed tool results are returned to your AI client and may be processed by its provider. Scope the data you expose as well as the actions you allow.

Practical answers

Google Cloud Logging connection questions

Use Test connection to isolate service access problems. Use Playground and Activity to inspect endpoint permissions and tool calls.

Must I upload a service account JSON key?

No. ADC is supported, and the connection can optionally impersonate a service account. A JSON key is an alternative credential source.

Can I force every query to one namespace?

Yes. Set Always add this filter to the namespace or resource condition. The connector applies that scope together with the agent’s query.

Does this use SQL?

No. A GCP Cloud Logging connection uses the Logging query language. The AI should form its filter for that backend.
